front.title: Sink-Attested Closure Evidence (SACE): Signed Epoch Acknowledgements and Accountable Revocation Closure

abstract.t: Revoking delegated authority in an agentic system is complete only when every place that can still act on that authority has stopped. Existing work defines the states of that process but leaves its evidence format open. This document defines Sink-Attested Closure Evidence (SACE): a small set of COSE-signed objects and one deterministic algorithm. An authority root signs a Scope Manifest naming the sinks a closure claim covers, and a Cut Statement raising the minimum admissible authority epoch. Each sink signs an Epoch Acknowledgement with its own key, binding the cut to the sequence number of the last effect it committed before applying it. Each committed effect yields a signed Effect Receipt. From these objects any party can compute one of three verdicts: CLOSED, UNKNOWN, or VIOLATED. A VIOLATED verdict comes with a transferable proof consisting of two signatures by the same sink. A sink that never acknowledges blocks CLOSED until it is removed from scope. An optional binding ties the acknowledging key to remote attestation evidence. This document makes no claim that a sink which signs an acknowledgement actually enforces it; it makes a sink that does not enforce it provably accountable for every effect it receipts.
